In [[mathematics]], specifically [[abstract harmonic analysis|harmonic analysis]], '''Harish-Chandra's ''Ξ'' function''' is a [[special function|special]] spherical function on a [[semisimple Lie group]]. It was introduced by [[Harish-Chandra]],{{sfnp|Harish-Chandra|1966|loc=section 16}} who used it to define [[Harish-Chandra's Schwartz space|his Schwartz space]].

For <math>K</math> a maximal [[compact space|compact]] subgroup of a semisimple Lie group with [[Iwasawa decomposition]] <math>G=NAK</math>, <math>g</math> an element of <math>G</math>, <math>a(g)</math> the element <math>a</math> in the Iwasawa decomposition <math>g=nak</math> and <math>\rho</math>  a [[Weyl vector]], the <math>\Xi</math> function is defined as

:<math>\Xi(g)=\int_Ka(kg)^\rho dk</math>.

[[Nolan Wallach|Wallach]] gives a detailed description of the properties of <math>\Xi</math>.{{sfnp|Wallach|1988|loc=4.5}}
